item.title: ★ A Survey of Uncertainty Estimation in Large Language Models
item.author: Grace Mensah, Daniel Kowalski
item.description:
95% · LLM calibration 95%

We review methods for uncertainty estimation in large language models, covering verbalized confidence, sampling consistency, and probe-based approaches. We organize the literature by the kind of prediction being scored and discuss open problems in calibration for long-form generation.

item.title: ★ Rerank Less, Retrieve Better: Query-Adaptive Depth for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.author: Samir Haddad, Elena Petrova
item.description:
95% · RAG & retrieval 95%

Retrieval-augmented generation pipelines typically rerank a fixed number of passages. We show that retrieval quality for question answering depends strongly on query difficulty, and train a lightweight controller that chooses retrieval depth per query. The controller cuts reranker calls by 58% while improving answer accuracy on four question answering benchmarks.

item.title: ★ TraceGrade: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Tool-Use Tasks with Step-Level Verification
item.author: Mira Okafor, Tomás Lindqvist, Hae-won Seo, Priya Raman
item.description:
95% · Agent evaluation 95%

Benchmarks for LLM agents usually score only the final answer of a multi-step episode. We introduce TraceGrade, a benchmark of 1,240 multi-step tool-use tasks across web, shell, and spreadsheet environments in which every intermediate action is verified against an executable checker. Evaluating 14 LLM agents, we find that final-answer accuracy overstates step-level correctness by up to 31 points. Code and tasks are publicly released.

item.title: ★ Calibrated Abstention for Language Model Question Answering via Conformal Uncertainty
item.author: Jonas Brandt, Aiko Tanaka, Lucía Ferrer
item.description:
95% · LLM calibration 95%, RAG & retrieval 35%

Language model predictions are often overconfident, which makes abstention unreliable. We propose a conformal procedure that turns token-level signals into calibrated uncertainty estimation for open-domain question answering. Across five datasets, our method reduces expected calibration error by 43% and lets the language model abstain with a guaranteed error rate.

item.title: ★ Position: Evaluating Autonomous Agents Needs Cost-Aware Metrics
item.author: Michael Brooks, Anika Sharma
item.description:
94% · Agent evaluation 94%

We argue that evaluating LLM agents by success rate alone hides the cost of multi-step tool-use. We propose reporting success per dollar and per minute and show how rankings on popular agent benchmarks change under cost-aware metrics.

item.title: ★ Do LLM Agents Know When They Are Wrong? Self-Evaluation of Tool-Use Trajectories
item.author: Laura Chen, Pedro Alves, Yuki Mori
item.description:
94% · Agent evaluation 94%, LLM calibration 68%

We study whether LLM agents can evaluate their own multi-step tool-use trajectories. Agents' self-reported confidence is poorly calibrated: across three agent benchmarks, trajectories rated 90% likely to succeed succeed only 61% of the time. A simple uncertainty estimation probe on hidden states recovers much of the gap.

item.title: ★ SciRetrieve: A Benchmark of Retrieval Quality for Scientific Question Answering
item.author: Oluwaseun Adeyemi, Clara Dubois
item.description:
93% · RAG & retrieval 93%

We release SciRetrieve, a benchmark of 9,800 expert-written scientific questions with passage-level relevance labels, to measure retrieval quality for retrieval-augmented question answering. Dense retrievers and rerankers still miss a supporting passage for 27% of questions.

item.title: ★ 4-Bit KV Cache Compression for Long-Context LLM Inference
item.author: Arjun Mehta, Sofia Rossi
item.description:
89% · Efficient inference 89%

Long-context LLM inference is dominated by KV cache memory. We introduce a 4-bit quantization scheme for the KV cache with per-channel outlier handling that keeps perplexity within 0.1 of full precision and enables 2.6x cheaper inference at 128k context.

item.title: ★ SpecTree: Draft Trees for Faster Speculative Decoding in Large Language Models
item.author: Wei Zhang, Olivia Grant, Rafael Moreno, Chen Li
item.description:
89% · Efficient inference 89%, LLM calibration 35%

Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by verifying draft tokens in parallel. We propose SpecTree, which drafts a tree of continuations and prunes it with a learned acceptance model. SpecTree delivers 3.1x faster decoding than autoregressive sampling with identical outputs, and composes with quantization for cheaper inference. Code is available.

item.title: Faster Decoding for Speech Language Models via Speculative Unit Prediction
item.author: Hyun-woo Park, Isabel Novak
item.description:
68% · LLM calibration 68%, Efficient inference 48%, RAG & retrieval 35%

Speech language models generate discrete units slowly. We adapt speculative decoding to unit sequences and obtain 2.4x faster inference with no loss in speech quality.
